children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares cut early gains on Thursday, as chipmakers turned lower amid worries about high bond yields and escalating conflict between the U.S. and Iran.
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed up 16.76 points, or 0.26%, at 6,579.48, after rising as much as 1.8% earlier in the session.
** During the session, the index briefly turned lower to fall as much as 1.9%.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
ended down 0.20% and peer SK Hynix
lost 1.05%, erasing early gains.

** "Risk-averse sentiment heightened across global markets with the yen suddenly strengthening sharply in afternoon trade amid bond yields already at high levels," said Seo Sang-young, an analyst at Mirae Asset Securities.

** Fears of renewed escalation gripped the Middle East on Wednesday after the United States and Iran exchanged their biggest barrage since July, with Washington striking Iran's southern coast and Tehran firing at U.S. bases across the region.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed 5.18%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were up 1.46% and up 2.41%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
added 3.64%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
fell 1.60%.
** Of the total 909 traded issues, 425 shares advanced, while 432 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 499.6 billion won ($367.68 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,359.3 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.01% lower than its previous close at 1,359.2.
** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.17 point to 103.12.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 4.6 basis points to 3.894%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 3.6 basis points to 4.368%.
